newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Helix shares continue to fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Helix shares continue to fall.

text.p: Shares in gold hopeful, Helix Resources NL continued to fall sharply on Wednesday, following the slump in the explorers share price on Tuesday on market disappointment with the company's latest drilling results.
At 10.35 a.m. (2335 GMT), Helix shares were 37.7 cents or 10.11 percent lower at A$3.35 on a volume of 141,300 shares.
On Tuesday, Helix shares ended A$1.26 or 25 percent lower at A$3.727 with 639,044 shares traded.
"Helix has got smacked again, down to A$3.30. With the negative press and the drill results yesterday that was to be expected," said broker Nick Atkinson of Brisbane brokerage Wilson HTM.

On Tuesday, Helix released results at its Timkillia prospect in the Gawler Craton region of South Australia from five new holes. The best result being a 44 metre intersection at an average of 2.6 grammes per tonne (g/t) gold.
The latest results had been eagerly awaited by the market after gold producer Acacia Resources Ltd acquired a 17.4 percent stake in Helix for about A$38 million last week.
At 10.45 a.m. (2345 GMT), Acacia shares were 3.1 cents lower at A$2.06 after falling nearly 10 cents to A$2.09.
